title: Navana.ai Raises Rs 40 Crore in Ronnie Screwvala-Led Round to Scale Voice AI
excerpt: The 2018-founded startup's speech models cover 12 Indian languages and 45 dialects, and the fresh capital will deepen its push into banking, financial services and insurance.
body:
• Voice AI startup Navana.ai has raised Rs 40 crore ($4.2 million) in a Series A round led by existing investor Ronnie Screwvala, the upGrad co-founder.
  • Antler India, Neysa.ai founder Sharad Sanghi, Avaana Capital's Sandeep Singhal and Paula Mariwala also participated in the round.
  • Founded in 2018 by brothers Raoul and Jai Nanavati, the company sells a full-stack, "sovereign" voice AI platform to banks and financial firms, with proprietary speech models covering 12 Indian languages and 45 dialects.
  • The capital will scale deployments across the BFSI sector, strengthen speech models and build an AI Contact Centre and automated evaluation platform; the company says it has serviced over 100 million voice AI minutes for clients including Bajaj Finserv and Ujjivan Small Finance Bank.

Voice AI startup Navana.ai has raised Rs 40 crore ($4.2 million) in a Series A funding round led by existing investor and upGrad co-founder Ronnie Screwvala, with participation from Antler India, Neysa.ai founder Sharad Sanghi, Avaana Capital partner Sandeep Singhal and Paula Mariwala, among others, according to Inc42 and The Hindu BusinessLine.

The round

Screwvala, who had already backed the company, led the round as voice AI emerges as one of Indian startups' busiest segments. Inc42 reported last month's raises by smallest.ai ($13 million) and Ringg AI ($15.5 million) as evidence of the sector's momentum. Screwvala pegs India's voice AI opportunity at about Rs 9,500 crore, though he noted that data localisation and regulatory compliance remain key considerations for enterprises deploying voice AI. "Navana.ai addresses exactly this, proving to be a reliable voice AI partner for India's enterprises," Screwvala said.

Context & Background

Navana.ai was founded in 2018 by brothers Raoul Nanavati, the CEO, and Jai Nanavati. Its founding thesis is that most Indians have been locked out of English-first digital services: only 6-10% of the population speaks English and just 38% of households are digitally literate, according to the company. Its answer is a sovereign, full-stack voice AI platform - voice agents, transcription systems and real-time analytics that enterprises can run on their own infrastructure, including on-premise deployments for regulated customers with strict data-control requirements.

Impact & Analysis

The traction is concentrated in banking, financial services and insurance, where call-center-driven processes - sales, collections, compliance and support - are being automated with voice agents. The company says it has serviced more than 100 million voice AI minutes for clients including Bajaj Finserv, Protean, Ujjivan Small Finance Bank, Jana Small Finance Bank and Grihum Housing Finance. Its proprietary speech models, built on real-world Indian speech, cover 12 Indian languages and 45 dialects and are designed to handle background noise, overlapping speech, code-switching and regional accents. The company also contributes to the wider ecosystem: with IISc Bengaluru it open-sourced RESPIN, a 10,000-hour speech corpus spanning 45 dialects, and it says its Bodhi model recorded the highest accuracy in a benchmarking exercise across Indian voice AI platforms using real-world speech samples.

"From day one, Navana.ai's mission has been to democratise access to digital services for every Indian, irrespective of where they live. India has spent the last decade building some of these critical digital rails, including identity, connectivity and payments. Now this next decade belongs to meaningful automation."

— Raoul Nanavati, Co-Founder and CEO, Navana.ai

Diaspora Angle

Navana.ai's Indic-language-first approach matters well beyond India: diaspora families increasingly interact with Indian banks, insurers and government services remotely, and voice systems that understand regional accents and code-switching make those interactions usable for older relatives back home who never adopted English-first apps.

What's Next

The fresh capital will deepen Navana.ai's BFSI footprint, sharpen its speech models for Indian languages and dialects, and accelerate product development on its AI Contact Centre and automated evaluation platform. The company plans to scale its sovereign voice AI infrastructure with what it describes as some of the biggest names in the BFSI industry.
nri_angle: Navana.ai's Indic-language voice AI makes Indian banks and services usable for relatives back home who never adopted English-first apps - a technology diaspora families increasingly rely on for cross-border interactions.
